market.question: Will the minimum Arctic sea ice extent this summer be less than 4m square kilometers?

assessment.reasoning: 2025 Arctic sea ice minimum was 4.60M km²; only 2012 (3.39M) and 2020 (3.74M) have been below 4M km² in the satellite record. 2026 spring extent and volume are at/near record lows entering melt season, raising the odds of a sub-4M minimum, but reaching it still requires an unusually warm/stormy summer. ~18% reflects elevated but still tail probability.
assessment.key_uncertainty: Summer Arctic weather (cyclones, persistent high pressure) drives most of the variance.
